newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says Swiss franc appreciation unjustified.
newsitem.headline: SNB says Swiss franc appreciation unjustified.

text.p: Bruno Gehrig, member of the Swiss National Bank's (SNB) council, said the current strength of the Swiss franc was unjustified and the appreciation had been caused by increased uncertainty about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We consider such an appreciation unjustified and reacted to it," Gehrig said in a speech to the bank's semi-annual news conference.
By increasing liquidity, money market rates have been eased and in this manner the SNB countered the upwards pressure on the Swiss franc, Gehrig said.
He did not make any comments on whether the SNB would continue to add liquidity or what the future policy could be.
Gehrig noted that since early March the external value of the Swiss franc had risen some 3.5 percent on a trade-weighted basis, reversing the weakening during the last year.
"The current strength of the franc is mainly due to the events and expectations of the European economic and monetary union," Gehrig said.

Signs that the German budget deficit would grow and the controversy over the Bundesbank's gold increased uncertainties over whether the Maastricht stability criteria could be rigorously maintained, he said, adding that the elections in France then also unsettled the markets.
"While the financial markets were confident for a long time, recent events paved the way for a more sceptical judgement," Gehrig said.
